zeal

/zeel/ — rhymes with feel · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Zeal is intense enthusiasm or eagerness in pursuing something.

She tackled the recycling project with such zeal that the whole school joined in.

Worked Example

The young activist displayed such zeal for environmental reform that she organized three campus cleanups in a single month.

The intensity here—the relentless drive to act—is exactly what zeal names. Because the enthusiasm is so focused and purposeful, zeal is more precise than the milder word 'interest.'

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fervor: Fervor is hot, intense feeling that pours out — the emotional temperature itself, glowing in speeches, prayers, and cheering crowds. Zeal is that heat put to work: eager, tireless effort in pursuit of a goal. A crowd can be full of fervor while standing still; zeal starts organizing.

devotion: Devotion is loyal, committed dedication to a cause or person — steady, patient, and long-term, proven over years of quiet service. Zeal burns faster and moves harder: eager, energetic pursuit that throws itself into action right now. Devotion endures for decades; zeal wants results this week.

gusto: Gusto is hearty, cheerful energy in the doing — you eat, sing, or paint with gusto, enjoying the activity for its own sake. Zeal is aimed at a goal or cause and keeps driving after the fun wears off. Gusto savors the moment; zeal serves the mission.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

apathy: complete lack of interest or feeling

indifference: not caring one way or the other

Where it sits · how much drive fuels the pursuit — interest → enthusiasm → passion → zeal

interest vs. zeal: Interest is the mildest step on this scale: being interested means you pay attention, while zeal means you pour your whole heart and energy into the pursuit.

enthusiasm vs. zeal: Enthusiasm is strong excitement, but zeal is stronger — enthusiasm cheers from the stands, while zeal signs up, organizes, and keeps working when everyone else quits.

passion vs. zeal: Passion is deep and powerful, yet zeal edges past it in drive: passion is the burning feeling, while zeal is that feeling converted into tireless, eager action.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — zel (zēlos)

Root — zel (zēlos): ardor, eager rivalry, noble passion (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Zeal comes straight from the Greek zēlos, 'ardor, eager rivalry' — the whole word is one root that has always meant this burning eagerness, so the root simply is the definition: intense enthusiasm in pursuing something.

Use the root in a new word: zealous

Use the root in a new word: zealous: The zealous fans camped outside the stadium for three days before the tickets went on sale — the same intense, eager devotion that zeal describes.

Word Choice

formal / literary

Zeal is the energy of purpose — reach for it when someone's enthusiasm drives them to action. For simple liking or interest, plain words like 'interest' or 'enjoyment' are simpler.
